reader.requirement: An OPEN naming several file-names (in one or several mode groups) acts as one separate OPEN per file-name in source order, each with its own group's mode, status and exception handling, so a failure of one file does not prevent the later ones and the earlier ones are done first.
reader.edition-search: read BindOpen and EmitOpen whole; grep Edition|CobolVersion|ConstructRegistry|DialectBehavior in both: the decomposition into BoundImplicitSeries of one BoundOpen per file is edition-free (the only ctx.Edition use is the rejection reporter)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers order with USE ending the run and mixed INPUT/I-O groups; not exercised: one file-name named twice in one statement, a failing file with no USE followed by later files, a relative file in the series

probes.expected: OPEN OUTPUT FA INPUT FA = OPEN OUTPUT FA then OPEN INPUT FA: the second is 41 (VII.1.3.5 4a) and FA stays open OUTPUT

reader.notes: BindOpen builds one BoundOpen per file-name in source order (BoundImplicitSeries) and EmitOpen opens, stores status and runs the USE hook per file. Probes show a same-file duplicate and a failure in the middle behave as separate statements.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR24 (cite.py OK) together with GR26 (status first, then USE, in that order; cite.py OK). The reader's probes never ran a USE that RETURNS between the file-names. r24_use.cob runs OPEN INPUT XA OUTPUT XB INPUT XC I-O XD with XA, XC and XD absent, a USE ON INPUT and a USE ON XD. It printed: USE-IN N=1 XA=35 XB=99 XC=99 XD=99; USE-IN N=2 XA=35 XB=00 XC=35 XD=99; USE-XD N=3 XA=35 XB=00 XC=35 XD=35; AFTER ... N=3. Each file's status is set and its USE runs before the next file-name is opened, exactly as separate OPEN statements in source order.
